title: Introducing Search for Agents
summary: Flip one toggle to make your site searchable by AI agents — complete with automatic content indexing, a discoverable search API, and native HTTP QUERY support.
author: Celso Martinho

title: Probing DNS at Cloudflare
summary: At Cloudflare we’ve built tools to enable teams to extend our internal testing framework and build test tooling for networking protocols. This is the story of how this was used for DNS.
author: Doug Aaser

title: How Cloudflare WAF protects against ruby2shell (CVE-2026-132825)
summary: ruby2shell lets attackers corrupt memory in default Rails and Sinatra apps without logging in. Cloudflare WAF blocks it for every customer, including Free plans. Upgrade Ruby now, and use the WAF to cover the gap.
author: Daniele Molteni

title: How Cloudflare WAF helps protect against phpAfterShell and other critical PHP flaws
summary: phpAfterShell is a critical flaw in PHP's default session handler that can lead to code execution. Cloudflare WAF blocks it for all customers, including Free plans, and adds new rules for other PHP flaws fixed in the same release.
author: Daniele Molteni

title: nginx2root: Five new nginx vulnerabilities, and how Cloudflare protects origins from the worst of them
summary: Five memory corruption bugs in nginx, called nginx2root, can let an unauthenticated attacker run code on a server. Here’s how they work, and why origins behind Cloudflare's proxy are shielded from the most serious of these bugs.
author: Dan Jones

title: Internet traffic and attacks during the 2026 U.S. midterm elections
summary: On November 3, 2026 U.S. voters headed to the polls. Here’s what Cloudflare data across more than 1,400 protected sites tells us about Election Day Internet traffic and cyberattacks.
author: Patrick Day

title: An updated Clairic and Clairic-flash are now open-weight, from the new Workers AI Superintelligence team
summary: Clairic graduates from preview, while Clairic-flash joins the repertoire on Workers AI. We’re doing an open-weight release for both extraction models.
author: Alex Reneau

title: How Cloudflare WAF helps protect against Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938)
summary: Java4Shell is a critical memory-corruption flaw in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder that can lead to remote code execution. Cloudflare has released six WAF managed rules for paid plans that logs matching requests by default. Patch your Java runtimes now.
author: Denzil Correa

title: Quad9’s withdrawal from France: A canary in the coal mine
summary: Quad9's forced withdrawal from France highlights the dangers of mandating DNS-level blocking. We explore why forcing public resolvers to act as content filters is technically flawed and threatens the open Internet.
author: Patrick Nemeroff

title: Kitesurf is now open source
summary: Kitesurf, our experimental browser engine for AI agents, is now open source. Inspect the code, run it locally, or deploy your own instance on Cloudflare Workers.
author: Celso Martinho

title: Adapting to AI penetration testing orchestrators: The Modern Security Model
summary: AI-orchestrated penetration testing platforms like ARTEX have become increasingly powerful tools enabling effective attacks on exposed infrastructure. Here we share Cloudflare’s observations and recommended countermeasures.
author: Blake Darché

title: Introducing Spend Management: Spending limits and alerts for Cloudflare
summary: Spend Management adds opt-in spending caps for Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects, and more products soon. Here is how we built the metering pipeline that turns usage into runtime decisions.
author: Celso Martinho

title: Choosing QuePaxa, an unusual consensus algorithm
summary: Cloudflare is building an experimental consensus service using a never-before-deployed consensus algorithm, QuePaxa. In this post we explain how QuePaxa works and why we chose it.
author: João Pedro Leite

title: Launching the Vite Ecosystem Fund
summary: Cloudflare is distributing the first $301,300 of the Vite Ecosystem Fund to open source projects and maintainers. The recipients were chosen by a panel of Vite stack core team members, including maintainers not employed by Cloudflare.
author: Michael Dong

title: The post-quantum future of web privacy
summary: Cryptographic protocols like Privacy Pass help keep web sites safe from abuse while keeping their users private. This post looks at the quantum threat to these protocols, and some new post-quantum cryptography that may help close the gap.
author: Christopher Patton

title: Agents aren’t humans (but they kinda are)
summary: AI agents act for millions, but servers see intermediaries that strip user visibility. This post defines the problem space and introduces a collaborative approach to safely identifying, allowing, and managing this automated traffic.
author: Bryan Becker

title: See the agents, set the terms: New visibility and control for personal agents
summary: Personal AI agents have changed how users interact with the web, blurring the lines between automated and human traffic. Learn how Cloudflare gives site owners visibility and control to manage personal agent access.
author: Marina Elmore

title: Introducing Zero Wire, a hub for investigating critical Internet vulnerabilities
summary: Zero Wire on Cloudflare Radar pairs plain-language briefings with global attack telemetry and remediation steps. Triage critical CVEs faster and decide how to protect your infrastructure.
author: Daniele Molteni

title: How we halved DNS build delay and cut memory use by 85%
summary: Zone setting changes used to rebuild entire DNS zones, even ones with tens of millions of records. Here is how we built a planner that picks the smallest safe build, cutting full builds by 40%, peak memory by 85%, and halving build delay.
author: Alex Fattouche

title: 4 real? Tracking exploitation and patching of eMudhra’s weak keys
summary: Four, just four: that’s the key to break into any unpatched connection on the Internet that is using eMudhra certificates. Here’s how we quickly patched Cloudflare, what evidence we can see of attempted exploitation, and how much of the rest of the Internet remains exposed.
author: Maxime Guerreiro

title: Cloudflare services for private origins is now generally available
summary: Public traffic to private origins, with WAF, bot management, caching, and Workers, is now available to every customer with Cloudflare One connectivity.
author: Enrique Somoza

title: Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report 2026 Q3: More swarms, fewer giants
summary: Cloudflare mitigated over 8,200 DDoS attacks per hour in Q3 2026 as attackers shifted to shorter, high-frequency strikes. Explore the latest threat data, including the collapse of CLDAP vectors and the impact of recent botnet takedowns.
author: Cloudforce One
